body.text: UKPNP International Conference on Jammu Kashmir in House of Commons UK — 8th July 2025

London, 8 July 2025 — The United Kashmir People's National Party (UKPNP) held a landmark International Kashmir Conference in the Boothroyd Room of the Houses of Parliament, London, under the theme: 'Kashmir Conflict: Peace, Security and Fundamental Rights in Jammu and Kashmir'. The conference saw extensive participation from Members of the British Parliament, international human rights activists, legal experts, academics, Kashmiri and oppressed nations' leaders, media professionals, and diaspora representatives.

body.caption: Panelists at the UKPNP International Kashmir Conference, House of Commons, London

body.text: Chief Guest and Keynote Speaker

body.caption: Sardar Shaukat Ali Kashmiri, Exiled Chairman of UKPNP, delivering keynote address at the House of Commons

body.text: Sardar Shaukat Ali Kashmiri, Exiled Chairman of UKPNP and Administrative Director of CIRAC to the United Nations (Geneva & New York), was the chief guest and keynote speaker. In his powerful address, he expressed sincere gratitude to Labour MP Richard Burgon for hosting this important conference, and to Fabian Hamilton for initiating this vital platform. He stated that UKPNP is honored to hold the 4th International UKPNP Kashmir Conference in the British Parliament, advancing peace, democracy, and human rights in South Asia. He said that UKPNP highly values the steadfast support of British colleagues for the forcibly divided people of Jammu and Kashmir, who are caught between three nuclear powers and suffer under extremism, terrorism, and counter-terrorism. He congratulated UKPNP United Kingdom for their continued efforts in organizing these impactful conferences.

From the outset, UKPNP has championed secularism, peace, democracy, and reunification of the historical State of Jammu and Kashmir, while categorically rejecting the use of religion as a weapon, all forms of extremism, terrorism, and proxy politics.

Due to this pro-people and pro-peace ideology, UKPNP has faced state persecution and was forced into exile but remains committed to its cause. Sardar Shaukat Ali Kashmiri strongly condemned the extrajudicial killings of Zarnosh Nasim and Jibran Nasim, two educated brothers from Bagh, Azad Kashmir, who were reportedly killed in a police operation in Rawalakot. UKPNP demands an independent judicial inquiry and full accountability for this grave human rights violation.

body.caption: Panelists at the UKPNP International Kashmir Conference, House of Commons, London

body.text: He also demanded the immediate and unconditional release of all peaceful political prisoners from across the entire State of Jammu and Kashmir, including Gilgit-Baltistan. Among those unjustly imprisoned are human rights defenders such as Mumtaz Nagari, Advocate Ehsan Ali, Advocate Taaruf Abbas, Sher Nadir Shahi, Muhammad Nafees, and others. Furthermore, he urged Pakistan and India to refrain from imposing unilateral decisions on the people of Jammu and Kashmir. The future of the region must be decided by its people through inclusive, democratic, and peaceful processes — not through force or external diktats.

Kashmir is not a territorial dispute between India and Pakistan — it is a matter of life, identity, and dignity for millions of Kashmiris. We demand freedom of expression, movement, reunification, and the right to self-determination for all.

Sardar Shaukat Ali Kashmiri urged Great Britain and the international community to support the establishment of a unified, independent buffer state of Jammu and Kashmir — one that serves peace and development in South Asia and denies its land for use in aggression against any neighbor. Let us be clear: Kashmir is not a territorial dispute between India and Pakistan — it is a matter of life, identity, and dignity for millions of Kashmiris. We demand freedom of expression, movement, reunification, and the right to self-determination for all. He urged Members of Parliament and the global community to remain engaged and committed to justice, peace, and human rights in Jammu and Kashmir.
Conference Host and Distinguished MPs

body.caption: Richard Burgon MP, Labour MP for Leeds East and Former Shadow Secretary of State for Justice Conference Host

body.text: The conference was hosted by Richard Burgon MP, Labour MP for Leeds East and Former Shadow Secretary of State for Justice. Other distinguished MPs present included Fabian Hamilton MP, Labour MP for Leeds North East and Former Shadow Minister for Peace and Disarmament; Imran Hussain MP, Labour MP for Bradford East and Chair of the All-Party Parliamentary Group on Kashmir; and Ian Byrne MP, Labour MP for Liverpool West Derby.

body.caption: Fabian Hamilton MP addressing the conference, reaffirming commitment to Kashmiris' right to self-determination

body.text: MP Richard Burgon emphasized that Kashmir is one of the world's longest unresolved conflicts, which must be resolved peacefully according to the will of the Kashmiri people. MP Fabian Hamilton stated that this conference should ideally be the last if it leads to peace, and committed continued support to Kashmiris' right to self-determination.

body.caption: Imran Hussain MP, Chair of All-Party Parliamentary Group on Kashmir, declaring Kashmir an international issue

body.text: MP Imran Hussain declared the Kashmir conflict as an international  not a bilateral issue  rejecting the relevance of the Shimla Agreement. MP Ian Byrne reaffirmed that self-determination is a fundamental right which Kashmiris deserve.

body.caption: Ian Byrne MP reaffirming that self-determination is a fundamental right which Kashmiris deserve

body.text: The conference was moderated by Sardar Nasir Aziz Khan, Central Spokesperson of UKPNP and Main Representative to the UN in Geneva and New York, and presided over by Sardar Tariq Khan, President of UKPNP United Kingdom.

body.caption: Panelists and Participants at the UKPNP International Kashmir Conference, House of Commons, London

body.text: Speakers and Representatives

The conference featured addresses from numerous speakers including Dr. Shabir Chaudhry, Writer and Senior UKPNP Leader; Representative of Mehran Marri, Prominent Baloch Leader and Human Rights Defender; Mahmood Ahmed Kashmiri, Chairman of the Jammu Kashmir National Independent Alliance (JKNIA) and UKPNP Senior Leader; Mrs. Faria Attique, Secretary of the Foreign Affairs Committee, UKPNP; Raja Sarfraz Khan, Secretary General, UKPNP; Sajjad Hussain, President, UKPNP London Unit; Sohail Talat, President, UKPNP Bradford Unit; Syeda Mahroona Bukhari, Vice President, UKPNP Bradford Unit; Syed Barkatul Hasan, Deputy General Secretary, UKPNP UK; Mushahid Manzoor, Deputy General Secretary, UKPNP Leeds Unit; and others.

Notable participants included Sardar Amjad Yousaf, Sardar Tikka Khan Tahir, Yasir Arfat Qureshi, Naveed Khan, Aftan Hussain, Jamil Latif, Farooq Nazir, Muhammad Ramzan, Ishaq Khan, Muhammad Gaffar Hussain, Irfan Ashfaq, Hamza Shakeel, Muhammad Nisar, Muhammad Anis, Shafique ur Rehman, Syed Altaf Hussain, Abdul Rehman, Gul Zaman, Muhammad Ijaz Khan, Mahmood Ahmed, Qamar Khalil, Abdul Satar, Zarak Aftab, Usman Khan, Muhammad Adnan Khan, Qamar Farooq, Iftikhar Waqas, Arif Ajakia, Syed Taqdees Ali Gilani, Mehtab Subhani, Muhamad Shehbaz, Syed Farzad Gilani, Saiq Shah, Abdul Aziz Sheen, Sohail Aqeel, Haidher Aftab, Ashfaq Sadiq, Raja Yasir Sayab, Ishtiaq Sadiq, Musa Sadiq, Salar Saeed, Maqsood Kiyani, Waqar Aziz, Shezad Afzal, Syeda Tousifa Haider Gilani, Malik Sajid Hussain, Maria Mehwish, Zohaib Khan, Hina Javaid, Raja Muhammad Habib, Moseeb Khan, Zaheer Ahmed Kiyani, Saqib Khan, Akash Khan, Hashir Abbasi, Muhammad Rukshad Khan, Naqeer Ahmed, and others.

body.caption: Large gathering of participants at the UKPNP International Kashmir Conference, House of Commons, London

body.text: Resolutions Adopted at the Conference

body.caption: UKPNP Activists and Diaspora Kashmiris attending the historic conference in London

body.text: Numerous resolutions were presented by Sardar Shaukat Ali Kashmiri and unanimously adopted at the UKPNP International Kashmir Conference in the House of Commons, London, on 8th July 2025, under the theme 'Kashmir Conflict: Peace, Security and Fundamental Rights in Jammu and Kashmir'.

items: We strongly condemned the heinous act of terror in Pahalgam, Kashmir, which claimed the lives of at least 26 innocent civilians and left many others injured. We offer our heartfelt condolences and unwavering solidarity to the families of the victims. We especially honor Adil Shah, who sacrificed his life while protecting tourists. We demand a transparent and independent investigation to ensure that the perpetrators of this crime against humanity are brought to justice.

During recent crises between India and Pakistan, dozens of innocent Kashmiris lost their lives on both sides of the so-called Line of Control (LoC). Homes and properties were destroyed or severely damaged, and thousands were displaced. We urge the United Kingdom, United Nations, and international community to ask both countries to take immediate steps to reinstate all displaced persons and compensate the families of the victims.

Reaffirm our unwavering commitment to the Universal Declaration of Human Rights, and call upon all parties involved in the Jammu and Kashmir conflict to end all forms of human rights violations, including arbitrary arrests, enforced disappearances, extrajudicial killings, and restrictions on freedom of expression, movement, and association.

Demand full, unrestricted access for international human rights observers, journalists, and humanitarian agencies to all parts of the historical State of Jammu and Kashmir, Ladakh, including Gilgit-Baltistan and so-called Azad Kashmir.

Affirm that the people of Jammu and Kashmir, in all its regions — Jammu, the Kashmir Valley, Ladakh, Gilgit-Baltistan, and so-called Azad Kashmir — are the primary stakeholders in the conflict and must be included in all dialogue and decision-making processes.
Call for the gradual and complete withdrawal of the armed forces from civilian areas on both sides of the Line of Control to protect the lives, dignity, and fundamental freedoms of the population.

body.caption: Participants raising awareness for Kashmir cause at the House of Commons

items: Urge the respective governments to instruct their security forces to immediately cease the use of torture, enforced disappearances, extrajudicial killings, and fabricated encounters.

Strongly condemn and express deep concern over the alarming rise in enforced disappearances and the kidnapping of minors in Azad Kashmir, Gilgit-Baltistan, and Pakistan. The United Kingdom should ask Pakistan to recover kidnapped children and hold the perpetrators accountable.
Demand an end to the arbitrary use of anti-terrorism and sedition laws to silence political dissent and suppress human rights activism.

Emphasize that the Kashmir conflict is not merely a territorial issue between India and Pakistan. It is fundamentally about the human rights, identity, future, and dignity of the people of Jammu and Kashmir — especially the right to self-determination, access to natural resources, and reunification of families divided since October 1947.
Call upon India and Pakistan to jointly establish humanitarian corridors and enable cross-border trade and travel to reunite families, promote regional peace, and foster people-to-people ties.

Stress that all regions of Jammu and Kashmir must be allowed to function within open, democratic, and secure environments, where political parties, human rights defenders, and civil society organizations can operate without fear.

body.caption: UKPNP supporters at the International Kashmir Conference demanding reunification

body.text: Condemnation of Extremism and Proxy War

body.caption: Delegates of UKPNP from various regions at the conference

body.text: The conference unequivocally condemned all forms of terrorism and religious extremism, whether perpetrated by state or non-state actors, and called on all authorities to take effective measures against groups or individuals that promote violence, radicalization, sectarianism, or hatred in the name of religion or nationalism. It asserted that no part of Jammu and Kashmir should be used to conduct proxy wars or to spread ideological radicalization.

On January 5, 2025, Azad Jammu Kashmir Prime Minister Chaudhry Anwar-ul-Haq chanted 'Al-Jihad, Al-Jihad' slogans in Muzaffarabad, instigating violence in Kashmir, and assured that the AJK budget would be allocated for jihad.

The conference expressed deep concern over the use of Azad Kashmir as a launchpad for extremist activities, where banned outfits are promoted, projected, and allowed to operate freely with impunity. Youth are being recruited and trained for the so-called 'Jihad' in Kashmir. Those who oppose this proxy war and militant agenda are often silenced or eliminated. Operation Tupac, Pakistan's proxy war in Kashmir conducted under the guise of jihad, resulted in the deaths of an estimated more than 150,000 people.

body.caption: Participants listening to speeches at the House of Commons

body.text: Call for Reunification and Buffer State Status

The UKPNP emphasizes the urgent need for the reunification of the erstwhile State of Jammu and Kashmir as a critical step toward sustainable peace, security, fundamental human rights, and stability in South Asia. Reunification is essential for fostering mutual understanding, reducing hostilities, and promoting constructive dialogue between India and Pakistan.

We believe that there is no military solution to this conflict. Forced divisions, annexations, and unilateral decisions imposed have only intensified suffering and hostility. The historical State of Jammu and Kashmir should be reunified and declared as a buffer state between three nuclear powers — India, Pakistan, and China.

A just and peaceful resolution and reunification must be based on UN resolutions on Kashmir and the democratic will of the people of Jammu and Kashmir. The conference declared that India and Pakistan have no legal right to annex, merge, or unilaterally determine the status of any part of the historical State of Jammu and Kashmir.

body.caption: Panelists and Participants at the UKPNP International Kashmir Conference, House of Commons, London

body.text: International Engagement and Diaspora Involvement

The conference appealed to the British Government, the United Nations, the European Union, and other international institutions to acknowledge the urgency of a just and peaceful resolution to the Kashmir conflict and to play a proactive role in supporting inclusive and rights-based peace processes. The conference recommended the appointment of a UN Special Rapporteur or independent international envoy to monitor and report on the situation across both sides of the Line of Control.

body.caption: UKPNP Activists and Diaspora Kashmir demanding Justice for Zarnosh Nasim and Jibran Nasim with banner in front of the House of Commons

body.text: The conference recognized and appreciated the positive contributions of the Kashmiri and South Asian diaspora in raising global awareness and advancing the cause of peace, justice, and democracy, and encouraged further inclusion of diaspora voices in shaping future peace frameworks. It recommended the creation of an International Kashmir Peace and Human Rights Working Group, coordinated by UKPNP and supported by British Parliamentarians and international human rights organizations, to monitor developments, propose practical solutions, and submit annual reports to the British Parliament.

body.caption: UKPNP Delegates and Participants at House of Commons United Kingdom

body.text: Concluding Remarks

UKPNP leadership thanked MP Richard Burgon for hosting the impactful conference and all MPs for their insights. Moderator Sardar Nasir Aziz Khan thanked MPs Richard Burgon and Fabian Hamilton, noting that this was the 4th consecutive international conference on Kashmir organized by UKPNP in the House of Commons. Special congratulations were extended to the United Kingdom Chapter of UKPNP for their remarkable efforts, dedicated coordination, and powerful presence in organizing this successful event.

Jammu and Kashmir is not a territorial or bilateral issue between India and Pakistan. It is an international issue. United Nations resolutions on Kashmir remain relevant and take precedence over the Tashkent and Shimla Agreements, or any other bilateral arrangements between the two countries.

The entire State of Jammu and Kashmir, including the Kashmir Valley, Jammu, Ladakh, Azad Kashmir, and Gilgit-Baltistan, constitutes one historical and political entity and remains disputed. India and Pakistan have no legal right to annex, merge, or unilaterally determine the status of any part of the historical State of Jammu and Kashmir. The people of the State of Jammu and Kashmir deserve their fundamental rights, including the right to free movement, the right to reunification of divided families, and the right to self-determination in accordance with international law and United Nations resolutions.

The future status of Jammu and Kashmir must be determined in accordance with United Nations resolutions and in line with the wishes and aspirations of the people of Jammu and Kashmir. Any decision imposed on the basis of majoritarianism or military force is illegal, constitutes a clear violation of United Nations resolutions on Kashmir and international law, and is unacceptable to the people of the disputed State of Jammu and Kashmir.

body.caption: Delegates and participants at the historic UKPNP conference in House of Commons

body.text: In conclusion, the UKPNP reaffirmed its peaceful and democratic mission for the reunification of Jammu and Kashmir. The event marked a significant milestone in uniting global voices for peace, justice, and fundamental rights in South Asia.
